task.title: Consolidate CLI scripts into single dispatcher
task.description: Refactor 25+ individual TypeScript CLI scripts into a single dispatcher architecture with unified entry point.
task.problem: The CLI scripts system has grown to 25+ individual TypeScript files, each compiled separately. This creates: - A 500+ character build:scripts command in package.json - Duplicate entry definitions (package.json overrides tsdown.config.ts) - 39 output files in .festinalente/scripts/ (scripts + chunks) - Maintenance burden when adding new commands (must update config files)
task.value: - Single entry point simplifies build configuration dramatically - Adding new commands requires only adding a function and registering it (no config file changes) - Cleaner CLI interface matching common patterns (git, npm, docker) - Removes configuration duplication between package.json and tsdown.config.ts - Reduced build complexity and output file count
task.acceptance-criteria:
Given the festinalente package is built When a user runs `node .festinalente/scripts/festinalente.cjs <command> [args]` Then the command executes and returns JSON output identical to the previous separate scripts
Given the build is run When tsdown completes Then dist/scripts/ contains festinalente.cjs (plus any chunk files for dependencies) And the 500+ character build:scripts command is removed from package.json
Given a developer wants to add a new command When they create a function in src/scripts/commands/ and register it in index.ts Then no changes to package.json or tsdown.config.ts are required
Given a user runs `node .festinalente/scripts/festinalente.cjs --help` Then they see a list of available commands
Given a user runs an unknown command When they execute `node .festinalente/scripts/festinalente.cjs unknown-cmd` Then they receive a JSON error response with available commands listed
